topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What must a person do before they can obtain a Minnesota motorcycle instruction permit?
choice_a: Hold a motorcycle endorsement in another state for at least one year
choice_b: Complete a skills test on a public roadway
choice_c: First pass a knowledge (written) test at a driver examination station
choice_d: Register the motorcycle before taking any test
explanation: A valid Minnesota driver's license is required to obtain a motorcycle instruction permit. To obtain the permit, you must first pass a knowledge (written) test at a driver examination station.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.II, 'Motorcycle Permit Process'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: How many times per day may a person take the motorcycle knowledge test?
choice_a: Only once per week
choice_b: As many times as they wish in a single day
choice_c: Exactly twice per day
choice_d: Only once per day
explanation: The knowledge test may be taken only once per day. When you pass the test and pay the $29 permit fee, you will receive an instruction permit valid for one year.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.II, 'Motorcycle Permit Process'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: How long is a Minnesota motorcycle instruction permit valid once issued?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: 30 days
choice_c: Five years
choice_d: Until the holder's next birthday only
explanation: When you pass the knowledge test and pay the $29 permit fee, you will receive an instruction permit valid for one year. If it expires, you must retake the knowledge test and pay the fee for a new permit.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.II, 'Motorcycle Permit Process'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: Under 2018 Minnesota law, where is a person with a motorcycle instruction permit allowed to ride that was previously off-limits?
choice_a: Any road at night without restriction
choice_b: The interstate highway
choice_c: Any road while carrying a passenger
choice_d: Roads with a speed limit above 70 mph only
explanation: Effective August 1, 2018, a person with a motorcycle instruction permit is allowed to ride a motorcycle on the interstate highway.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.I, 'New Riding Information and Laws'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: While riding on an instruction permit, what restriction applies regarding passengers?
choice_a: Passengers are allowed only in a sidecar
choice_b: The permit holder may carry one passenger only
choice_c: The permit holder may not carry passengers
choice_d: There is no passenger restriction on an instruction permit
explanation: While operating a motorcycle with an instruction permit, the rider may not carry passengers, must wear a DOT-approved helmet and eye protection, and may not ride at night.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.II, 'Motorcycle Permit Process'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: Applicants under 18 years old must present what before taking the motorcycle knowledge test?
choice_a: A completed skills test scorecard
choice_b: A notarized letter from their employer
choice_c: Proof of motorcycle ownership
choice_d: A certificate of completion of a state-approved motorcycle rider training course
explanation: If you are under 18 years old, you must also present a certificate of completion of a state-approved motorcycle rider training course before taking the knowledge test.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.II, 'Motorcycle Permit Process'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: The motorcycle endorsement skills test consists of how many riding exercises?
choice_a: Four
choice_b: Ten
choice_c: One
choice_d: Twenty
explanation: The skills test consists of four riding exercises that measure vehicle control and hazard response skills; the two-wheel and three-wheel versions are administered on the same course.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.II, 'Motorcycle Endorsement Skills Test'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: Why won't the motorcycle skills test be administered on a given day?
choice_a: If the temperature is above 80 degrees
choice_b: If the test surface is wet, or ice or snow is present
choice_c: If more than one applicant is scheduled that day
choice_d: The skills test is always given regardless of surface conditions
explanation: The two-wheel and three-wheel skills tests are administered on the same course and will not be given if the surface is wet, or if ice or snow is present.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.II, 'Motorcycle Endorsement Skills Test'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: If a new Minnesota resident already holds a valid out-of-state driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement, what may happen to the road skills test requirement?
choice_a: New residents are exempt from the knowledge test but must always retake the skills test
choice_b: The skills test can never be waived under any circumstance
choice_c: The motorcycle skills test will be waived when the applicant passes the knowledge test
choice_d: New residents must retake both tests regardless of their out-of-state endorsement
explanation: A new Minnesota resident with a valid motorcycle endorsement from another state (or one expired less than a year) needs to take a knowledge test to get a Minnesota license; the motorcycle skills test will be waived when the applicant passes the knowledge test.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.III, 'New Residents'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What is the motorcycle instruction permit/endorsement fee listed in the manual's fee schedule?
explanation: The motorcycle instruction permit/endorsement fee is $29.00, according to the manual's Motorcycle Fees schedule; fees are set by law and subject to change.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.III, 'License Fees'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What additional fee is added when renewing a Minnesota driver's license that carries a two-wheeled motorcycle endorsement?
choice_a: A $17 motorcycle endorsement fee
choice_b: A $50 endorsement renewal surcharge
choice_c: No additional fee is charged at renewal
choice_d: A $200 late fee regardless of timing
explanation: When your Minnesota driver's license has a two-wheeled motorcycle endorsement, you will pay the license fee plus a $17 motorcycle endorsement fee when you renew your license with your endorsement.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.III, 'Endorsement Renewal'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What is the annual registration period for motorcycles in Minnesota?
choice_a: January 1 through December 31
choice_b: March 1 through the last day of February
choice_c: July 1 through June 30
choice_d: Registration never expires once issued
explanation: The registration period is from March 1 through the last day of February. Re-registration is required annually and expires at the end of February.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.III, 'Motorcycle Registration'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: How many days does a new Minnesota resident have to register their motorcycle after becoming a resident?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: 10 days
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: There is no deadline for new residents
explanation: New residents have 60 days after becoming Minnesota residents to register their motorcycles.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.III, 'Motorcycle Registration'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What insurance coverage must all motorcycles registered in Minnesota carry?
choice_a: Only theft coverage is mandatory
choice_b: Comprehensive coverage for the motorcycle's own damage, mandatory in all cases
choice_c: No insurance is required for motorcycles
choice_d: Liability coverage for property damage or injury to another party
explanation: All motorcycles registered in Minnesota must have liability insurance coverage for property damage or injury to another party; no-fault, uninsured motorist, and damage/theft coverage are optional.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.III, 'Motorcycle Insurance'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What can happen to a motorcycle operator's registration and license if they do not carry the required liability insurance?
choice_a: The Commissioner of Public Safety may revoke the registration and suspend the license
choice_b: Nothing -- there is no consequence for lacking insurance
choice_c: Only a small fine is issued, with no effect on registration or license
choice_d: The motorcycle is automatically donated to the state
explanation: The Commissioner of Public Safety may revoke the registration and suspend the license of any motorcycle operator who does not carry the required insurance.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.III, 'Motorcycle Insurance'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: Which item is required as basic safety equipment for every Minnesota motorcycle in addition to lights?
choice_a: A passenger backrest
choice_b: A rearview mirror, horn, and muffler
choice_c: A tachometer
choice_d: A GPS navigation unit
explanation: All motorcycles must have basic safety equipment in working condition -- in addition to a rearview mirror, horn, and muffler, motorcycles must be equipped with required headlights, taillight, footrests where applicable, and at least one brake.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.IV, 'Motorcycle Equipment Requirements'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What color and size accent is legally permitted on a motorcycle's red taillight in Minnesota?
choice_a: No colored accents of any kind are permitted
choice_b: A green dot up to three inches in diameter
choice_c: A blue dot up to one inch in diameter
choice_d: A flashing white strobe
explanation: Motorcycles must have one red taillight, including brake light/stop lamp. A blue dot of up to one inch in diameter on the taillight is legal.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.IV, 'Motorcycle Equipment Requirements'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: Under Minnesota's operating rules, may an operator ride a motorcycle between lanes of moving or stationary traffic headed the same direction?
choice_a: Yes, if a passenger is not on board
choice_b: Yes, at any speed under 20 mph
choice_c: Yes, but only during daylight hours
choice_d: No -- operators may not ride between lanes of traffic moving in the same direction
explanation: Operators may not ride a motorcycle between lanes of moving or stationary vehicles headed in the same direction.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.IV, 'Motorcycle Operating Rules'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: Under Minnesota's operating rules, what restriction applies to carrying packages or articles while riding?
choice_a: Operators may not carry packages or articles that interfere with keeping both hands on the handlebars
choice_b: Packages may only be carried in a backpack, never in hand
choice_c: There is no restriction on carrying packages while riding
choice_d: Packages are permitted only if under one pound
explanation: Operators may not carry packages or articles that interfere with keeping both hands on the handlebars.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.IV, 'Motorcycle Operating Rules'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What does the Basic Rider Course (BRC) skills-test waiver allow for a rider 18 or older who holds a motorcycle permit?
choice_a: Skipping the knowledge test entirely
choice_b: Earning a motorcycle endorsement upon successful completion of the skills test given at the end of the course
choice_c: Riding without any permit at all
choice_d: Automatic issuance of an endorsement with no testing of any kind
explanation: A rider 18 years of age or older who has a valid motorcycle permit can earn a motorcycle endorsement upon successful completion of the skills test at the end of the Basic Rider Course -- this is the skills test waiver. Riders younger than 18 are required to take the BRC before taking the state knowledge and skills tests.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.VIII, 'Basic Rider Course (BRC)'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What may a person who holds a motorcycle road guard certificate do during a group ride?
choice_a: Waive the knowledge test for other group members
choice_b: Issue traffic citations to other riders
choice_c: Operate as a flagger and stop and hold vehicles in place to direct motorcycles through an intersection
choice_d: Register motorcycles on behalf of the group
explanation: A person who holds a motorcycle road guard certificate may operate as a flagger and stop and hold vehicles in place to direct motorcycles within a group ride through an intersection; drivers stopped by a flagger may only proceed if instructed by the flagger or a police officer.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.VIII, 'Motorcycle Road Guard'

topic: Earning Your License and Licensing Process
question: What is the retesting fee for a third or subsequent knowledge test after failing the first two attempts?
choice_c: There is no fee for retesting
explanation: The manual's fee schedule lists a $10.00 retesting fee for a third and subsequent knowledge test (after failing the first two), available at driver exam stations only.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.III, 'Retesting Fees'
